name: Trap Bar Squat
description: A squat movement performed with a trap bar (hex bar), where the handles are at hip level and the lifter stands inside the frame. The trap bar's geometry allows a more upright torso than a traditional barbell back squat and shifts loading to the quadriceps and glutes, with reduced shear force on the lumbar spine.

execution.starting_position: Stand inside the trap bar with feet shoulder-width apart and the bar centered around your body. Grip the handles.
execution.setup_instructions: Load the trap bar on the floor. Stand inside it, feet shoulder-width, handles at mid-thigh. Hinge to grip the handles.
steps: Step 1: Brace your core hard, chest up, and drive through the floor to stand.
Step 2: Extend the hips and knees simultaneously to rise from the bottom.
Step 3: Lock out fully at the top with hips and knees extended.
Step 4: Lower the bar back to the floor with control, maintaining a neutral spine.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before the pull. Exhale at the top.
common_mistakes: Squatting with excessive forward torso lean (turning it into a deadlift pattern)
Allowing the knees to cave inward
safety_considerations: The trap bar squat is excellent for beginners — the neutral grip is easy to learn
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at lockout. Lower under control — do not bounce the plates off the floor.
